title: The Next Stage Of The LLM Race
gist: The cheap-Chinese-open-weights versus expensive-US-closed-models framing is breaking down as both camps move to tiered pricing strategies; open-weight models are taking low-cost token volume and edging into near-frontier work while the premium frontier holds, so value may shift toward owners of compute, cloud, proprietary data and enterprise distribution.

themes.theme: Pricing by tier, not by origin

insights.claim: The popular framing that pits cheap Chinese open-weight models against expensive US closed models is losing analytical value because both sides are adopting tiered strategies, so LLM pricing is now defined by model tier and business strategy rather than where a model came from.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Stop segmenting AI exposure by country-of-origin narratives; compare vendors on tier positioning and monetization strategy instead.
insights.quote: LLM pricing is increasingly defined by model tier and business strategy rather than a model’s origin.

themes.theme: Where the value accrues as costs fall

insights.claim: As falling model costs expand adoption, value may increasingly shift toward companies that control compute, cloud infrastructure, proprietary data and enterprise distribution rather than the model developers themselves.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Favor infrastructure, data-owning and distribution-controlling names over pure model vendors as inference prices deflate.
insights.quote: As falling costs expand adoption, value may increasingly shift toward companies controlling compute, cloud infrastructure, proprietary data, and enterprise distribution.

insights.claim: The decisive open questions are whether US labs can push the frontier fast enough to preserve premium pricing, and whether Chinese labs can convert adoption into durable revenue that funds continued frontier development.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Two testable watch-items: US frontier release cadence versus price realization, and Chinese labs' revenue conversion from usage share.
